tooltip.title: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis (LABD)
tooltip.markdown: A rare autoimmune disease characterized by linear deposition of IgA at the basement membrane zone. It has both idiopathic and drug-induced forms.

tooltip.title: Pathophysiology of LABD
tooltip.markdown: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of linear IgA bullous dermatosis

tooltip.title: Target Antigens
tooltip.markdown: IgA autoantibodies target proteolytic fragments of BP180 (LAD-1, LABD97)

tooltip.title: Mechanism
tooltip.markdown: IgA deposition recruits neutrophils, leading to a subepidermal split

tooltip.title: Clinical Features of LABD
tooltip.markdown: Key clinical manifestations and physical findings

tooltip.title: Classic Lesion
tooltip.markdown: Tense vesicles and bullae arranged in an annular or "string of pearls" configuration

tooltip.title: Childhood Form
tooltip.markdown: Often presents as Chronic Bullous Disease of Childhood with prominent involvement of the lower abdomen and perineum

tooltip.title: Adult Form
tooltip.markdown: More widespread involvement of trunk and limbs. Mucosal involvement is common

tooltip.title: Histology
tooltip.markdown: Subepidermal blister with a neutrophil-predominant infiltrate

tooltip.title: Direct Immunofluorescence
tooltip.markdown: The gold standard. Shows linear IgA deposition along the basement membrane zone

tooltip.title: Salt-Split Skin
tooltip.markdown: Antibody binding usually to the epidermal side (roof) of the split

tooltip.title: Treatment of LABD
tooltip.markdown: Therapeutic approaches for linear IgA bullous dermatosis

tooltip.title: Second Line Treatment
tooltip.markdown: Systemic corticosteroids, colchicine, or immunosuppressants like Mycophenolate Mofetil
